messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

We need to parse the problem carefully.

The problem:

We have a fictional lost-sales inventory system. Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity). Any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout is a strictly positive unmet demand, not simply ending with zero stock.

We need to simulate historical events up to target_time, with knowledge cutoff. The system receives reports (eligible_events) that have received_time (the time when we become aware of the report). We only keep those with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Within that, for each event_id there can be multiple revisions; we choose the highest visible revision (i.e., highest revision number) for each event_id among those visible (i.e., whose received_time <= cutoff). That revision replaces earlier ones, not additive.

Then we keep chosen events whose event_time <= target_time (i.e., actual occurrence times). Then we apply those events in order sorted by (event_time, event_id) (if ties, event_id lexical order perhaps). Starting from initial_stock, we compute the stock state at each step. We track historical lost (i.e., sum of unmet demand) for all events up to target_time.

Then we need to compute stock_at_target = the stock after processing all historical events up to target_time, i.e., the stock after applying them.

We also need to compute historical_lost = total lost quantity from historical events (presumably up to target_time).

Then we get the "future_schedule" events (these are a hypothetical scenario). After reconstructing the historical state, apply every event in future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order (starting from the reconstructed stock). Note that future events start after target_time (but might have event_time <= horizon_time). Actually target_time is 100, horizon_time is 130, the future_schedule's event_time range: starts at 101 up to 118. So these are after the target time, within horizon.

Apply them. Compute stock_at_horizon after processing all future events (the final stock after applying them). Also compute future_lost = total lost from demand events in the future scenario only (i.e., sum of unmet demand for future events). Also compute first_future_stockout_time = earliest event_time among future events where there was unmet demand (i.e., demand > stock at that point, resulting in positive lost). Or -1 if none.

We must return these five integers via submit_answer.

Edge Cases: There might be historical events up to event_time <= target_time (100). The known cutoff is also 100. So we only have reports with received_time <=100. But there may be some reports with event_time <=100 that are not visible because their received_time >100 (i.e., after cutoff). Those must be excluded from reconstruction entirely.

Thus we need to filter eligible_events to those where received_time <= knowledge_cutoff (100). Among those, pick the highest revision per event_id. Then from those selected events, keep only those with event_time <= target_time (100).

We then sort them by (event_time, event_id). Process them.

We need to compute lost for each demand event: lost = max(0, quantity - stock_before). stock_before = current stock before processing the demand. After demand, stock becomes max(0, stock_before - quantity). Note that if quantity > stock_before, then we have unmet = quantity - stock_before. Lost = unmet. Stock goes to 0.

For receipt events: Add quantity. Even if quantity = 0, just do nothing.

Also need to track historical_lost across all historical demand events up to target_time (which is also the same set we apply as historical events). Then after that, stock_at_target is the stock after processing those events.

Now, after reconstruction, apply future_schedule events. These also consist of receipts/demands. We apply them in order: sort by (event_time, event_id). The event_id are given as "F-00" etc. They are strings that will be compared lexicographically probably. We need to confirm the ordering: primary sort by event_time ascending; for ties, secondary sort by event_id ascending. Since all event_times are distinct in this schedule (101, 102, etc.) ordering is just by event_time.

When applying future events, we track lost (unmet) for each demand event; sum to future_lost. Also track if ANY demand has unmet >0, record its event_time; we want earliest of those event_time (lowest) among future events. If none, output -1.

After applying all future events, we output stock_at_horizon: final stock after applying all future events.
